name: Communication Services
scope: Telecommunications, media, entertainment, and interactive communication platforms.
questions: How are subscriptions, advertising, content, and network spending connected?
Which distribution channels or platforms control customer access?

name: Consumer Discretionary
scope: Consumer businesses whose demand is sensitive to income, confidence, and discretionary spending.
questions: How sensitive is demand to employment, credit, and consumer confidence?
What drives brand strength, inventory risk, and distribution economics?

name: Consumer Staples
scope: Essential consumer goods, household products, and related retail distribution.
questions: How much growth comes from pricing versus volume?
How do private labels, input costs, and distribution affect margins?

name: Energy
scope: Energy exploration, production, equipment, services, refining, and transportation.
questions: Where does the company sit in the energy value chain?
How do commodity prices, production, hedges, and capital intensity interact?

name: Financials
scope: Banking, insurance, capital markets, and other financial services.
questions: Which interest-rate, credit, underwriting, or market exposures matter?
What capital and liquidity constraints limit growth or distributions?
metrics: Net interest margin or underwriting result

name: Health Care
scope: Health care providers, equipment, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, and related services.
questions: What clinical, regulatory, reimbursement, and patent events change the outlook?
How dependent is the business on individual products or programs?

name: Industrials
scope: Capital goods, transportation, aerospace, defense, and industrial or professional services.
questions: How do orders, backlog, capacity, and delivery timing translate into cash?
Which supply bottlenecks, contracts, or end markets determine profitability?

name: Information Technology
scope: Software, technology services, hardware, semiconductors, and related equipment.
questions: What connects end demand to pricing, recurring revenue, and capacity?
Which switching costs, ecosystems, and technological changes affect competition?
metrics: Recurring revenue and retention where relevant

name: Materials
scope: Chemicals, metals, mining, construction materials, packaging, and forest products.
questions: How do supply, demand, commodity prices, and input costs interact?
What resource, process, or logistical advantages support economics?

name: Real Estate
scope: Property ownership, equity REITs, development, and real estate services.
questions: Which property types, tenant exposures, and lease structures drive cash flow?
How do funding costs, occupancy, and supply affect asset values?

name: Utilities
scope: Electric, gas, water, and related utility infrastructure and services.
questions: How do regulation, allowed returns, and rate cases affect investment recovery?
What connects demand growth, generation mix, and funding needs?
